chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf from Muthanna ibn al-Walid al-Hannat from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked, 'A woman leaves her husband [dying without other heirs],' he said, 'All the wealth is his, if there is no other heir for her besides him.'
ai.seo_question: What does a husband inherit from his wife if she has no other heirs?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the husband's status as the sole inheritor when a wife dies without descendants or ascendants, a ruling derived from the general principle that the spouse is the primary heir in the absence of closer kin. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the husband’s share is not limited to the fixed quarter or half but expands to the entirety of the estate when no other heirs exist, reflecting the comprehensive nature of his inheritance right in this specific scenario. This hadith serves as a key textual evidence for the application of *al-‘Asabah* (residuary inheritance) principles to spouses in Shia fiqh.
